Ah ok I'm with you now. I actually just opened the chart, and it had all happened already - price was sat at the edge of the bounce, formed a nice big inverted pin on M1, and I took it. The strength of the level we bounced from initially made me take the trade, although I did wonder if it might go deeper. As it happened, it was off the D1 zline nicely.

I too am a bit impatient with RTs, and quite often get in too early, end up holding stubbornly, and then it turns out not to be a RT, and in fact just a continuation of the move! Generally I will try to identify the possible RT levels, and then watch for M1 PA as it enters each zone. I want to see a sharp move or CP into the zone, followed by a couple of pins or dojis before I will take it. If price starts forming a flag just below my possible RT level, I won't touch it until the flag is broken back the other way, as all too often these become the DP that breaks the zone against you.

If it makes it all the way to the edge of the initial move, then again I'll watch for PA and take it if it looks promising, and probably go back into the history to find any possible FO zones.

And don't worry, you're not spamming, all discussion is helpful!

author: smimon
text:
Eng or FO?

Here's something which was puzzling me for a while, the number of times that a FL appears to have been engulfed, only for the move to continue in its original direction -seemingly a "failed engulf".

In terms of a bullish move, consider that many times a FL forms just after a FTR is momo'd over, or ignored. When price retraces later, and appears to have engulfed our FL, in actual fact what has happened is that it has dipped slightly lower to bounce off the ignored level that the FL formed above.

This will of course be clearer with an example. Here's a recent one on EU.

It may be the case that there's something on the tick chart in these occasions, but I don't have the data.

I'm not going to treat any eng of a few pixels as a real eng - there are too many reasons why it might be FO. When a genuine eng happens, it's usually by a lot more than a pip or two - and even if you miss a few valid ones, you'll keep yourself out of a lot of bad ones too.

author: charlespips
text:
Hi Smimon,

Sorry to intrude your journal, but I was puzzled by this one as well when answering Knight's question in IF's journal. Do you think that the mini FL which has been engulfed is unimportant, so the engulf of it can be ignore and the one at the bottom is actually and engulf, not a FO to MPL level?

Kindly share your analysis. I'm still learning about FL and struggling to understand which FL is more important when digging into LTF.

As for Eng or FO, Isn't that ENG must happen first, signaling the turn, then FO will appear for liquidity reason? So the order is: ENG, and then FO. If there is no ENG, then no FO.

Hey pal. They're both indicators I wrote, I strangely enough really enjoy coding for MQL, I've pretty much know it inside out after getting enraged at it for the last 10 months!

The marker one shows news events, past and present, that are applicable to the pairing you're looking at. I use a javascript bookmarklet to parse the calendar from FxStreet into a text file, and the indi reads it.. Different colours dependent on the expected volatility, future events shown with a dotted vline so I don't forget what's in store for the week, could also add alerts, although haven't done so yet.

The line one is just a simple one - if you double click on the chart above or below any candle, it will draw a fibo line from the top or bottom wick, with the line period and date of the candle on it. You can toggle whether you want the line to be drawn from the candle wick or the candle body with a hotkey.

I'm actually considering writing some commercial indis to raise a bit of spare cash, I'm halfway through implementing the functionality of Forex Tester in MQL, so it'll work straight inside MT4.

Let me know if you want either of those ones, I can email them over to you.

Cheers

author: smimon
text:
First journal update of the new year, so I'll take the opportunity to wish you all a Happy New Year.

So my first 3 months with the RTM material were a real ray of light in the darkness of the "trading without a clue" wilderness that had come before. I'd gained the ability to make some great trades, but was still haemorrhaging losers all over the place. After once already revisiting all the material once from scratch, I decided to read through the RTM thread on Forex Factory to see if I could glean any further nuggests from it. It's a great read, I recommend it to anyone who hasn't seen it yet. The main thing I picked up was the importance of FLs above all else. So many times a seemingly strong FTR gets taken out, only for you to then realise we just went deeper into the FL that caused it. In particular, this sentence from IF about FOs struck home and made a lot of sense - "Say price is coming up to a supply. The only way we can be sure that supply will hold price down is if that supply has already visited the extreme set of orders in the flag limit to its left. If the supply fell short of that, we can anticipate a FO to those extreme orders." (the link to the thread is here by the way - www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=420159 )

With this information in mind, and resolving that this year I will turn this trading style into a science, rather than an art, I'm trying to take fewer trades, and analyse the charts as thoroughly as possible to spot the important FLs, and engulfs thereof. I'm sure I'll still get some wrong, but I aim to get those down to the utter minimum. It really is possible not to take any full stop outs if you know what you're doing.
